title.narrative: Psychosocial project & integrated livelihoods, related to the exit period of CAFOD funding

description.narrative:
The 1994 Tutsi genocide, subsequent flight, displacement, imprisonment and poverty within the Rwandan society have greatly been at the basis of currently observed psychosocial problems. As a result, phenomena such as destruction of social values, of loss of community and family solidarity, domestic violence in families both nuclear and extended, disputes on properties, material, and land possession have increased. Financial and technical support would tremendously facilitate further the project in trauma healing and reconciliation and in preventing and reducing poverty and related social conflicts through improved livelihood of beneficiaries.
The support to the CDJP’s previous efforts and interventions would assist in enhancing skills and knowledge of community volunteers, in increasing beneficiaries’ livelihoods and promoting participation and collaboration of different stakeholders, including local administrative leaders.
In this regards, the current project will built on the previous project’s achievement in the area of promotion of social cohesion and reconciliation through different interventions in conflicts resolution and trauma healing. Indeed the previous project achieved remarkable results but with limited scope and depth, given the complexity of the social economic situation involved beneficiaries are involved into on a daily basis, and the number of people in need of similar support. This project comes reinforce the initiated efforts and maintain and increase community livelihood through increased dialogue between the different categories of people conflict for the promotion of social justice geared towards the promotion of wealthier and reconciled people within assisted communities.
On the pathway to 2012-2013 , year of closure of activities of the program, and in line with the project, the Justice and Peace Commission of Kigali Archdiocese will operate in all the diocese of Kigali and especially in the two 2 districts: Nyarugenge and Rulindo that started in 2010.
The project will cover most of parishes of rural area of the Kigali Archdiocese. The Justice and Peace Commission will be implemented through a network of volunteers based at decentralized structures of the Church. Interventions will include community sensitization on Rwandan civil and criminal laws, sensitization on trauma prevention and healing, identification and support in resolving social injustice cases and promotion of community advocacy. To address the socio-economic aspects of conflicts and violence within households and communities, the Justice and Peace Commission will identify and support individual household beneficiaries’ income generating activities that affect trauma healing recovery sustainability.
The project will work on the continuity of the psychosocial program’s results of CAFOD-Rwanda.
